messages:
devin: heads-up — after the device-plugin rollout to v0.18 in us-west1 we started seeing training pods Pending and a bunch of NCCL connectivity errors in the logs. impact: some dedicated pool jobs falling back to general nodes and higher cost.

maria: logs? which nodes / error snippets pls

devin: quick excerpts:

```
kubectl describe pod gpu-train-01
Status: Pending
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/30 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't have free GPUs, 20 node(s) had no matching nvidia driver.
```

And from one of the failing pods:

```
NCCL ERROR Unhandled cuda error, driver mismatch
ncclCommInitRank failed
```

Also `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows a subset of nodes in us-west1-b reporting capacity 0 for nvidia.com/gpu briefly during the rollout.

sanju: deploy-bot shows the rollout completed ~15:22 UTC for us-west1. infra-bot, do we have canary metrics? we should check whether driver daemonset restarted at the same time as plugin.

infra-bot: canary rollout: device-plugin v0.18 → 100% in us-west1 at 2026-02-12T15:22:18Z. Driver daemonset restarted on 12 nodes during the window (non-uniform).

devin: suspicious part — some nodes had kernel updates last night (kernel 6.1.x) and the nvidia kernel module didn't get rebuilt on them, so /dev/nvidia* was missing. v0.18 changed the init handshake: it now proactively advertises 0 capacity if it can't bind devices, so scheduler started treating those nodes as GPUless and reshuffled pods — some moved to nodes that *did* have devices but the container runtime was still using an older driver (race), leading to NCCL driver mismatch.

lee: that matches a thread I saw on the driver team. v0.18 added a short probe that queries the kernel module version before exporting resources. If the kernel module is absent it marks the node as gpu=0 instead of waiting for driver-daemonset to recover. Good for correctness but caused a scheduling race during the simultaneous driver restart.

olivia: any quick mitigation to stop churn and cost spike? we have Dedicated reservations running out and jobs getting dispatched to on-demand nodes.

sanju: rollback device-plugin in the region to v0.17 (pining) + cordon/repair approach for nodes without /dev/nvidia*.

maria: agreed. plan:
1) rollback device-plugin to v0.17 in us-west1 canary first (deploy-bot: `helm rollback gpu-device-plugin 1 --namespace gpu-system`) 
2) cordon affected nodes and `kubectl delete pod` to force scheduling on stable nodes
3) run `dkms autoinstall` / restart driver ds on nodes missing modules
4) resync and re-enable plugin v0.18 after module-rebuild verification and add a short rollout pause

devin: I'm starting the rollback now in us-west1-canary and tagging ops-runbook #gpu-driver-regress

deploy-bot: rolling back chart gpu-device-plugin to revision 1 in namespace gpu-system — started.

maria: commands that helped to triage:
```
ssh node-xxx
sudo modinfo nvidia || echo "no module"
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200
kubectl -n gpu-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin
```

lee: long-term: we should add a pre-rollout check that verifies kernel module presence across nodes before forcing plugin update. Also add a rolling window where plugin waits for driver-daemonset to signal healthy on each node (handshake ack).

olivia: also put a temporary routing policy to prefer Dedicated pools with pinned model_variants so we don't spill jobs to more expensive pools during remediation.

sanju: noted — infra action items:
- rollback v0.18 in us-west1 (in progress by devin)
- add preflight script to release pipeline to check /dev/nvidia* and `nvidia-smi` on sample nodes
- schedule a maintenance window to rebuild DKMS on nodes with kernel 6.1.x
- add a canary pause and health-gate between device-plugin and driver DS in helm chart

devin: rollback done for us-west1-canary, monitoring for Pending -> Running numbers. will escalate to full-region rollback if greenlight.

maria: thanks. please add logs for the affected node list to the runbook and notify SRE oncall for the maintenance window.

olivia: thumbs-up. keep cost/product teams in the loop — I'll post a brief note in #customer-impact if jobs keep spilling.

lee: small follow-up — check NCCL errors for version skew between container CUDA toolkit and host driver; sometimes newer containers tolerate older drivers up to a point, but we saw hard failures here.

devin: will collect a small pack of `nvidia-smi` + `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` + container `nvcc --version` for a handful of failing pods and attach to the runbook.

sanju: assign to infra:me to own the preflight and to driver-team:triage for kernel module automation. meeting set in 30m to sync.

olivia: :thumbsup:
